title: Test Coverage Gap Review (periodical run): delta vs 2026-10-23 — verify LIN-690/LIN-3798 closures by mutant and CI history, re-check zero-coverage + fake-only high-cost modules, feed area notes (coverage + reliability)
description:
## As asked

<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="test-coverage-gap-review" -->

**Periodical: Test Coverage Gap Review** (advisory, review-only). This run reviews the Harbour test suite's **coverage and reliability**. It measures the change since the 23 Oct report and records what it finds in a report plus area-note entries, in **one docs-only PR**. It files **no follow-up tickets**. Remit source: `generateTestCoverageGapPrompt`, `lib/periodicals.js` (`id: 'test-coverage-gap'`).

Repo: `JKershaw/LinearViewer` (Harbour). When this was minted, `origin/main` was `da5df707d`, **476 commits** after the previous report's write commit. Re-ground against live `main` when you start: every path and status below is a pointer to check, not a finding.

## 0. Audit the scope before executing

Treat this scope as a starting point. Before running anything, look for surfaces this remit covers that this ticket does not name, and add them. Widen what you *examine*, not what you *report*. The report is uncapped and severity-ranked, and a near-empty clean result is a real outcome. Note entries are written only where a finding binds a builder or leaves work waiting in an area, and each note stays under its cap. Candidates the minting pass saw but did not size:

* **Sibling repo** `JKershaw/simple-dispatcher`**.** The last run recorded it but did not grade it: 3,471 tests at 96.86 / 90.81 / 89.14, two tests failing only under instrumentation, and CI running only `npm test`. LIN-3160 is now Done. Decide whether to grade it this time, and state the decision either way.
* **Unit coverage served by fakes.** The earlier run left open a census of high-cost `lib/*-store.js` modules whose unit coverage comes only through an inline fake (C3 was the one instance it found). LIN-3541, "replace hand-written DB fakes", is Todo.
* **Untested** `urlKey` **filters.** The Security Review (10 Nov) left an entry in `docs/areas/agent-api.md` saying the `urlKey` filters in `routes/proxy-model-routing.js` are untested. That is a coverage gap sitting on a security seam. Grade it here, cite the entry, and do not duplicate it.
* **High-cost modules new or heavily changed in the window.** For example, `lib/account-erasure.js` was not mutation-spiked last time, and `lib/dispatch-store.js` has scattered error branches.

## 1. Read prior runs first

* Previous report: `docs/reviews/test-coverage-gap-2026-10-23.md` (LIN-3797). Research ran at `f81f472b` and the report was written at `0b5afa6f`. Measure the delta from `0b5afa6f`. Baseline report: `docs/reviews/test-coverage-gap-2026-06-25.md`. Evidence folders follow the `docs/reviews/_evidence-<date>[-tag]/` pattern.
* Start from its **Trend Ledger** and diff against it by stable name. Ticket states seen at mint time, to re-verify:
  * `dispatch-token-store-untested-auth-boundary` (High): **LIN-690 is now Done**. Re-run mutants M3 (`revokeToken` drops `urlKey`) and M5 (`listTokens` leaks `tokenHash`). Mark the item resolved only if both are now KILLED.
  * `e2e-retry-hidden-dispatch-api-stray-queue-item` and `…collective-fanout-seat-failure`: **LIN-3798 is Done**. Use CI history to check whether `tests/e2e/dispatch.spec.js` "Dispatch API" and `tests/e2e/collective.spec.js` retry rescues have actually stopped since it merged.
  * `harbour-feedback-tokens-zero-coverage`: LIN-2061 is Backlog, and `lib/harbour-feedback-tokens.js` changed in the window. Re-check whether it is still missing from the coverage table (Trap 1).
  * `proxy-fetch-egress-untested`: LIN-1879, an open defect inside the uncovered lines, is Backlog.
  * `real-mongo-suites-skip-silently`: LIN-3799 is Backlog.
  * `agent-status-grouping…`: LIN-691 is Canceled. Check whether the dead `listSessions` / `listTaskThreads` methods were deleted. `lib/agent-status-store.js` changed in the window.
  * The Lows: proxy-tokens idle prune (M14), the never-run skip at `tests/e2e/interactions.spec.js` (R4), `lib/custom-prompts-store.js`, the error branches in `routes/openrouter-auth.js`, and `lib/harbour-spawn.js`.
* Re-check its **"Not done"** list as well. Do not re-flag anything that is already handled.

## 2. Run the review (coverage)

* **Ground truth** is the native coverage report. Add no coverage dependency. Build the command from `package.json` `test:unit` and `scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs`. Last time that was:
  `node --experimental-test-coverage --test --test-concurrency=N tests/unit/*.test.js scripts/eval/eval-dense.test.mjs scripts/code-shape/*.test.mjs`.
  * If you bypass the wrapper, blank `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENROUTER_FREE_TIER_KEY` yourself, as `unitTestEnv` does.
  * Set `MONGODB_TEST_URI` if you can, or the real-Mongo suites skip silently. CI uses `mongodb://localhost:27017` (`.github/workflows/test.yml`).
  * `CLAUDE.md` lists the hermetic variants (`test:hermetic`, `:proxy`, `:keyed`) and `test:clock-shift`.
* Read the **per-file uncovered lines**, not only the summary percentages. Weight each gap by what an untested defect would cost: error and failure handling, auth and token boundaries (proxy and dispatch tokens, feedback tokens, grants, owner gates), quota, money and rate-limit logic (free tier, plan allowance, the proxy limiters), and data integrity (stores, erasure, CAS). These classes are a starting list. Find the full set this remit covers from the repo.
* Avoid the three traps:
  * A module with **zero** coverage is missing from the table. Diff `lib/**` and `routes/**` against the parsed table.
  * A low percentage can mean the module is covered by Playwright (`tests/e2e/`).
  * Full line coverage can still hide an unasserted branch.
* **Evidence bar:** a coverage verdict names a defect the suite would or would not catch. The mutation-spike method from the last run is the model: apply a named mutant, run the unit files that import the module, record KILLED or SURVIVED. Any proposed fix must call for **behavioral** tests that assert outcomes (return values, thrown errors, observable state). Assertion-free tests and tests that only exercise the mock do not count. A higher percentage alone is never a win.

## 3. Fold in reliability signal (capability-gated)

At mint time CI history was reachable: the repo is public, `gh` is authenticated, and the last 40 `test.yml` runs were green. See `docs/architecture/ci.md`.

* Find what the history actually exposes and mine it. Last run found that the only per-test signal is:
  * the Playwright `list` reporter's `N flaky` block, plus the first-attempt `✘` and its error;
  * `retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0` in `playwright.config.js`;
  * `test-results/`, uploaded only on failure.
* Do not claim finer granularity than that.
* Check: flaky specs and retry rescues since `0b5afa6f`, `run_attempt > 1` re-runs, real-Mongo suite execution, and conditional `test.skip` sites that never assert.
* A reliability finding must name a concrete way the suite misleads, such as a regression a retry would turn green. A raw rate is not a finding.
* If CI history is unreachable when you run, **say so in the report** and continue with coverage only.

## 4. Mind the altitude

Report only the *test suite's own* trustworthiness. Leave these to their owners:

* project-wide churn convergence → **Stability Review** (latest `docs/reviews/stability-review-2026-11-08.md`);
* defect-escape clustering and fix-on-fix work → **Recent Headwinds** (`docs/reviews/recent-headwinds-review-2026-10-21.md`);
* dependency and supply-chain risk → **Dependency & Supply-Chain Review** (`docs/reviews/dependency-supply-chain-review-2026-11-10.md`);
* test *maintainability* (e.g. T-mockcoll in `docs/reviews/code-quality-review-2026-10-12-tests.md`) → **Code Quality**.

Cite a sibling only where its observation is evidence about whether the tests can be trusted.

## 5. Write an uncapped report

* Path: `docs/reviews/test-coverage-gap-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`, following the series convention. Put any evidence in `docs/reviews/_evidence-<date>-coverage/`.
* Rank findings by severity. Ground every `file:line` against the source at your HEAD, not against earlier reports.
* Keep a **Trend Ledger** with stable names so the next run can diff against it.

## 6. Feed the area notes and file no follow-up tasks

* Follow the notes' own rules, in `docs/areas/README.md`:
  * the registry is `docs/areas/areas.json`, first match wins;
  * each note has `## Lessons` and `## Waiting`;
  * the guard is `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js`, with a **6144-byte cap**;
  * the one-home rule is `LEFTOVER_RULE` in `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`.
* **Start with what changed.** List `git diff --name-only 0b5afa6f HEAD` and map each file to its area. Changes per area at mint time: runs-and-dispatch 82, front-end-pages 74, front-end-browser 73, llm-and-prompts 56, web-routes 37, auth-accounts-and-workspaces 31, agent-api 27, other-features 21, reports-and-operator-tools 13, providers 11, platform-and-plumbing 7, task-model 2, wiring 1. Read those areas first.
* **Caps are tight.** `docs/areas/agent-api.md` (\~6124 bytes) and `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` (\~6136 bytes) are almost at the cap. Prune settled or untrue entries before adding any. `providers` and `task-model` have no note yet. A new note must be named after the slug.
* Use a Waiting entry for work left in an area and a Lesson for a rule builders must follow. Each entry cites the area's file first. Its source is "(Test Coverage Gap Review, <date of this run>)", with the report as the second cited path. Cite files, never line numbers.
* A finding that already has a ticket (LIN-2061, LIN-1879, LIN-3799, …) stays in the report only, not in a note.
* **Findings with no area note:**
  * A larger tidy goes in as a Waiting entry worded as a size of move, and is also listed for the person.
  * A finding with no area file to cite (lockfiles, a live secret) goes in the closing comment, addressed to the person.
  * A cross-area seam is filed under the area a change would start from, naming the other side. Say in the report that seams have no full home in the notes yet.
* Commit the report and the note edits together in **one docs-only PR**, branch `docs/lin-<this-id>-test-coverage-gap-review-<date>`. Rebase it onto main and get it green under the notes guard and `ci-success`.

## 7. Stay review-only

Change no code, config, tests, or secrets. Touch no docs except the report, its evidence, and the area notes. Mutation spikes are local and get reverted; record them in the report.

## 8. Fresh-context adversarial second read (required)

* After the report and notes are written, and before hand-off, a separate reader answers cold: *"what is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"*
  * **Tier 1** (preferred): a wholly separate session.
  * **Tier 2** (accepted): a fresh-context sub-agent.
  * **Tier 3** (a self-re-read) is **not accepted**.
* Post **one** comment on this task with all three lines:
  * `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE|DISAGREE`
  * `Differed from top finding: YES|NO`
  * `Disposition: fixed in place|escalated|no change`
* Copy the same fields into a `## Adversarial Second-Read` section of the report, with the tier used, the question, and the reader's full answer.
* A DISAGREE verdict *is* the escalation. It never holds up the hand-off.

## 9. Hand off; do not merge or set Done

1. As soon as the PR is open, post its full URL as a comment on this task.
2. After the second-read comment, post a closing comment. It gives a concise, severity-ranked summary with the report path, names the PR, and lists for the person any larger tidy and any finding with no area file.
3. The closing comment states who finishes: review approves, then close-out merges, sets Done, and posts the final summary.

Leave the task **In Progress** and the PR rebased and green. If the PR cannot go green, name the blocker in the closing comment.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** Delivers the full asked review of coverage and reliability since the last report, with its report and area-note entries in one docs-only pull request; no Survey or area-note finding binds on it, and every pointer still holds.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Implementation Plan

Implemented and merged. The plan was carried out as approved, with two recorded deviations: the CI census was date-sliced (1,188 runs, 355 sampled) to get past `gh`'s 1,000-run cap, and the second read raised model-routing `urlKey` filters (C2) to the High/top finding.

* **fits one session**
* plan-review due: no. It is docs only, loosens no guard or contract, touches no credentials, merge rules or dispatch contract, routes around no cause, and is a single-session build.

## Outcome (close-out, 11 Nov)

* **Merged:** PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2397](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2397>), merge commit `30a01928961b90132287e5daffab9192b4b76f65`, deployed (Harbour footer shows `30a0192`). CI was green on head `9ea0c4116`.
* **Delivered:** `docs/reviews/test-coverage-gap-2026-11-11.md`, the evidence in `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-11-coverage/`, and Waiting entries in the agent-api (two pruned), front-end-pages, reports-and-operator-tools, platform-and-plumbing, runs-and-dispatch and web-routes notes.
* **Rulings applied:** LIN-690 was reopened (Todo), with M3 and M5 as acceptance tests, and its `docs/areas/agent-api.md` entry was removed (one home). LIN-3815 now covers the GitHub task-facts egress. LIN-3799 is narrowed to a census for new real-Mongo suites.
* The research findings, plan detail and revisions are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

## Research notes: LIN-4418 Test Coverage Gap Review (research stage, 11 Nov)

**Grounding.** Measured at `da5df707d` (= the mint sha, 476 commits after `0b5afa6f`). Since the ticket was created, live `origin/main` has moved by one docs-only merge, `fe2f1f0cb` (LIN-4413 Onboarding review). That merge touches only `docs/reviews/` and three area notes (`front-end-pages.md` is now 5,200 B, `auth-accounts-and-workspaces.md` 2,081 B, `front-end-browser.md` 2,734 B). No code citation below moves; the build must rebase onto it before editing notes. This stage wrote nothing to the repo. Every mutant was applied in a throwaway worktree and reverted, and the worktree was then removed.

### 1. Ground-truth run (Phase 2 command, re-derived)

Command, from `package.json` `test:unit` plus `scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs`, with the keys blanked as `unitTestEnv` does and real Mongo on:
```
OPENROUTER_API_KEY= OPENROUTER_FREE_TIER_KEY= MONGODB_TEST_URI=mongodb://localhost:27017 \
node --experimental-test-coverage --test --test-concurrency=5 \
  tests/unit/*.test.js scripts/eval/eval-dense.test.mjs scripts/code-shape/*.test.mjs
```
Node v25.9.0.

| | `0b5afa6f` (last report) | `da5df707d` (this run) |
|---|---|---|
| Tests | 19,272 local (CI 19,296) | **24,922; 24,921 pass, 1 fail** (real-Mongo suites included) |
| Line / branch / funcs | 95.97 / 87.60 / 92.35 | **95.01 / 88.71 / 91.08** |

The one failure is an environment artefact, not a product signal (see L5): `scripts/code-shape/wrappers.test.mjs:258` assumes no `node_modules` above `tmpdir()`. In dispatched sessions, `TMPDIR` sits under the simple-dispatcher checkout, which has acorn installed.

### 2. Mutation spikes (the evidence bar)

Method as in the last run: apply one named mutant, run every `tests/unit` file that names the module, and record whether any test fails. A control (a no-op comment edit) passed 748/748 first, which validates the harness.

| # | Mutant | Files / tests | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| M3 | `DispatchTokenStore.revokeToken` drops `urlKey` (`lib/dispatch-tokens.js:246-249`) | 26 / 748 | **SURVIVED** |
| M5 | `listTokens` adds `tokenHash` (`lib/dispatch-tokens.js:205-226`) | 26 / 748 | **SURVIVED** |
| M3p | sibling `ProxyTokenStore.revokeToken` drops `urlKey` (findOne + deleteOne) | 59 / 1,476 | KILLED (`tests/unit/proxy-tokens.test.js:672`) |
| M5p | sibling `ProxyTokenStore.listTokens` adds `tokenHash` | 59 / 1,476 | KILLED (`proxy-tokens.test.js:641`) |
| M25 | `DELETE …/dispatch/tokens/:tokenId` drops `refuseNonOwner` (`routes/dispatch.js:1173`) | 110 / 2,468 | KILLED |
| M17 | feedback token: drop the `expiresAt` filter | 114 / 2,401 | "KILLED", but only because the inline fake dereferences `query.expiresAt.$gt` (`tests/unit/harbour-feedback-tokens.test.js:18-19`): a fake-shape artefact |
| M17b | feedback token: `expiresAt: {$gt: new Date(0)}` (expired tokens accepted, query shape kept) | 114 / 2,401 | **SURVIVED** |
| M18 | feedback token: `itemId` binding dropped (`lib/harbour-feedback-tokens.js:97-99`) | 114 / 2,401 | **SURVIVED** |
| M19 | feedback token: `used:false` dropped (replayable) | 114 / 2,401 | KILLED (`harbour-feedback-tokens.test.js:34`, `lin-4198-usage-routes.test.js:355`) |
| M20 | model-routing preset apply drops `urlKey` (`lib/model-routing-store.js:222`) | 50 / 1,526 | **SURVIVED** |
| M21 | model-routing undo drops `urlKey` (`:233`) | 50 / 1,526 | **SURVIVED** |
| M22 | `listPresets` drops `urlKey` (`:161`) | 50 / 1,526 | **SURVIVED** |
| M23 | `getLog` drops `urlKey` (`:142`) | 50 / 1,526 | **SURVIVED** |
| M24 | `readTakenForUsage` drops `urlKey` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:3367`) | 80 / 2,124 | SURVIVED, partly equivalent: rows with `takenByTokenId` are token-scoped (`ownershipFilterOf`, `:472-476`), so `urlKey` is the only guard just for legacy label-keyed rows |
| M14 | proxy-token idle prune deletes recently used tokens (`lib/proxy-tokens.js:1058`) | 59 / 1,476 | **SURVIVED** (unchanged) |
| M26 | erasure: drop the `FOREIGN_SIGHTING_APPEARED` re-check (`lib/account-erasure.js:911`) | 7 / 407 | KILLED |
| M27 | erasure: drop the `PLAN_MISMATCH` check (`:877`) | 7 / 407 | KILLED |
| M28 | erasure: shared-anonymisation `arrayFilters` matches every element (`:932`) | 7 / 407 | **SURVIVED** |
| M29 | erasure: `idPrefix` regex unanchored, no `::` (`:306`) | 7 / 407 | SURVIVED, near-equivalent (account ids are UUIDs) |
| M30 | erasure: drop the `UNMAPPED_WORKSPACES` gate (`:878`) | 7 / 407 | KILLED |
| M31 | dispatch-store cleanup deletes un-archived rows (LIN-3805, `lib/dispatch-store.js:1728-1732`) | 158 / 3,319 | KILLED (behavioural, `lin-3805-store-fault-503.test.js:257`) |
| M32 | `getItemWatchToken` swallows a store fault (`:1256`) | 158 / 3,319 | KILLED, but by a source-shape census (`lin-3805-store-fault-503.test.js:677`), not behaviourally |

### 3. Reliability: CI history (reachable)

* `gh` is authenticated and the repo is public. 1,000 `test.yml` runs from 2026-10-24 to 11-11 (all after LIN-3798's merge `cada192e0`, 10-23 17:21Z): 947 success, 53 failure, 15 with `run_attempt > 1`.
* Sample: every 4th green run (237) plus every failed or re-run run (65). That gave 299 runs and 1,495 filtered job logs (1,196 e2e shards). The granularity is the same as last time: the `list` reporter's `✘` first attempt, the `N flaky` block, and the first-attempt error. `test-results/` is uploaded only `if: failure()` (`.github/workflows/test.yml:133-136`); `retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0` is at `playwright.config.js:22`.
* **LIN-3798 verified:** there are **0** `✘` lines for `tests/e2e/dispatch.spec.js` or `tests/e2e/collective.spec.js` in any sampled run. Both `e2e-retry-hidden-*` items are **resolved**.
* **The rate did not move:** 80 of the 246 sampled green runs (33%) still carry at least one retry rescue, the same as last run's 33%. New sites took the old ones' place. Rescues in green runs, by test site (count of runs):
  task-page.spec.js:376 (17), :379 (15), :374 (2): one test across line moves, **34 runs, 10-30 to 11-11, still occurring**. lin-3833-home-first-page.spec.js:98 (11, 10-25 only). session-proposals.spec.js:64 (**10, 11-02 to 11-08**). proxy.spec.js:59 (6, 10-25 to 26). lin-4010-home-opened-task.spec.js:227/230/339/342 (12; ticket **LIN-4102**). local-provider.spec.js:246/305 (6, 10-24 to 26). dispatch-page.spec.js:1133/1142/1171 "can revoke token" (6, 10-24 to 25). observation.spec.js:519/543 (2 each). Once each: lin-3968-home-next-step:332, observation-rulings:1148/1275, task-page:817, ship:332, live-console:3215.
* First-attempt errors:
  * task-page phone layout: `both offers on one line`, expected < 4, received 10.25, at `tests/e2e/task-page.spec.js:321`. A one-shot `boundingBox` read.
  * session-proposals: `[data-testid="session-run-chat"]` not found in 5 s, at `tests/e2e/session-proposals.spec.js:73`.
  * dispatch-page revoke: `settings-key-dispatch` count expected 0, received 1, at `:960`. That is exactly what a revoke no-op looks like, though it was seen only on 10-24 and 10-25.
* **Unit re-run rescues.** The last report said a unit flake "would show as red". In fact, manual whole-run re-runs act as a retry layer. 4 of the 15 re-runs had a **unit** job fail on attempt 1:
  * `tests/unit/db-indexes.test.js:771` failed 3 times, on 10-25 and 10-26, once on a `main` push. It was fixed in the window by LIN-3985 (`96efd1fe6`, 10-31).
  * `tests/unit/scheduler.test.js:265` "(e) error containment" failed once (run 40251525217, 10-26) with `expected the interval to keep ticking past the first throw (at least 2 calls), got 1`. The test sleeps 300 ms of wall clock, and its failure message is **identical to the defect it guards** (the interval cleared after a throw). It has not been fixed and has no ticket. LIN-4294 is the sibling `task-mode-routes` fixed-sleep case.
* **Live egress from e2e (new member of the LIN-3815 class).** `tests/e2e/settings-providers.spec.js:142,199` seed a GitHub binding (`octo/repo`) with a fake installation token. The background task-facts refresh (`lib/task-facts-holder.js:150`) then calls `api.github.com` live. `Bad credentials` appears in 126 sampled e2e logs (630 lines), on REST `/repos/octo/repo/issues|milestones` and on GraphQL. LIN-3798 stubbed Linear's `test-token` only (`routes/test.js:60`). LIN-3815 (Backlog) names the OpenRouter catalog and uploads.linear.app, not GitHub. The e2e run has no egress guard (the unit suite has `test:hermetic`). This is not proven to cause any rescue.
* **Real-Mongo skip (R3), a correction.** All 7 real-`mongod` suites (`mongo-smoke`, `scheduler`, `cost-read-usage-parity`, `dispatch-store-decision-withdrawal`, `lin-3130-taken-by-token-id-mongo`, `lin-3134-grant-declaration-mongo`, `lin-4198-request-usage-mongod`) **throw when CI is set and the URI is missing**. The guard was already in `tests/unit/mongo-smoke.test.js` at `0b5afa6f` (line 48 then, `:53` at HEAD). I verified it: `CI=1 MONGODB_TEST_URI=` gives fail 1 for mongo-smoke, scheduler and lin-4198. So the last report's "if the env line were dropped, CI stayed green" was wrong. The residual is that the guard is a per-file convention: no census makes a *new* real-Mongo file carry it. LIN-3799's scope could narrow to that census. The CI env lines are now at `test.yml:69,88`.
* **R4 unchanged:** `tests/e2e/interactions.spec.js:467` (skip at `:475`) is skipped in 2 of 2 full green logs. Playwright reports it as `:493` in a 490-line file.

### 4. Trap checks

* **Trap 1:** the absent set has shrunk from 11 to **1** (`routes/test.js`, mounted only under `NODE_ENV=test`). **The trap changed shape:** formerly absent modules now appear as *import-only rows*, with declaration lines counted but almost no functions run. Rows with funcs below 50%: `lib/render-audit.js` 0, `lib/render-custom-prompts.js` 0, `lib/render-templates.js` 0, `lib/custom-prompts-store.js` 14.3 (C8), `routes/legacy-redirects.js` 28.6, `lib/dispatch-session-read.js` 44.4, `routes/ship-biscuit.js` 45.5. None is on a high-cost path. The method must add this sweep, because a line percentage of 30 to 60 no longer means "executed".
* **Trap 2/3 and fakes:** C3 moved from Trap 1 to "covered through a fake" (see the fake census in §5).

### 5. Classes (bound and members)

1. **Cross-workspace / binding filters on token and credential stores** reached by proxy or dispatch routes. Bound: the stores the ticket and Security Review row 21 name, plus their proxy sibling; I did not sweep every `urlKey` filter in all 62 DB modules. Members:
   * `lib/dispatch-tokens.js`: M3 S, M5 S
   * `lib/proxy-tokens.js`: M3p K, M5p K, M14 S
   * `lib/harbour-feedback-tokens.js`: M17b S, M18 S, M19 K
   * `lib/model-routing-store.js`: M20–M23 S
   * `lib/dispatch-store.js` `readTakenForUsage`: M24 S, partly equivalent
2. **DB modules with no real-engine unit test** (fake-only). Bound: a script over the 62 `lib/**` modules that call collection ops. It lists the modules where no test file that imports them directly also imports `@jkershaw/mangodb`, `mango-tmpdir` or `mongodb`.
